summary: This diff claims to close four real round-1 bypasses of the interactive-session write gate, but live reproduction against the actual shipped snippet (ai-os/OWNER_DIRECTIVES/interactive-session-guard.bashrc-snippet) shows the round-2 hardening's central security claim is false and two of the guard's own new checks have real coverage gaps; the diff is additive-only (new files, no .github/workflows/** changes) and tier1 classification is correct, but it should not be merged as a genuine security control until these are fixed.
issues: CRITICAL, empirically reproduced: the 'kernel-verified, cannot be spoofed' cgroup signal is fully spoofable by the exact same account the guard is meant to restrict. _interactive_guard_cgroup_path() reads whichever file path is written into '$guard_dir/_cgroup_path' (a plain, user-writable file inside ~/.claude-interactive-session-guard.d/), not a hardcoded /proc/self/cgroup. Any interactive session can do: echo '0::/system.slice/veridian-worker@fake.service' > /tmp/x; echo /tmp/x > ~/.claude-interactive-session-guard.d/_cgroup_path; export INVOCATION_ID=anything; git push origin master -- and the push goes through to the real git unblocked. I reproduced this live against the shipped snippet: normal push to master was BLOCKED, then after only overwriting this one file (no root, no namespace tricks), the identical push was NOT blocked (real git was invoked). This is the exact same class of bug as round-1's 'export INVOCATION_ID=anything' bypass that this task claims to have fixed -- it just moved the spoof target from an env var to a file. The doc's comment 'It is not an environment variable, so it cannot be spoofed the way INVOCATION_ID can' is false; the seam should not exist in the production code path at all (it should only be reachable via a controlled test harness, e.g. an env var that is never set outside the test script, not a runtime-readable config file inside the very directory the guard installs into).

Empirically reproduced: 'git push origin +master' (standard git force-push refspec shorthand, equivalent to --force origin master) is NOT blocked. _interactive_guard_git_push_verdict() strips 'refs/heads/' but never strips a leading '+' force-push marker from the refspec, so dest ends up as the literal string '+master', which does not match the case pattern 'master|main'. Verified live: the push reached the real (faked) git binary unblocked.

Empirically reproduced: multi-refspec pushes only check the first refspec. 'git push origin feature-branch master' pushes both refs in one invocation, but _interactive_guard_git_push_verdict() only inspects positional[1] (the first refspec, 'feature-branch') and ignores any further positional arguments, so the protected 'master' ref in the same command is never evaluated and the whole push (including master) goes through to the real git unblocked. Verified live.

None of these three gaps are disclosed in the PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml 'known_limitations' section or the snippet's own KNOWN LIMITATIONS comment block, which only mention the same-account limitation and the absolute-path/`command -p` bypass -- the write-up is not fully honest about the guard's actual coverage, which matters more than usual here since this is a governance/security control other autonomous merges will be gated on.
No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff, so the hard workflow-scope rule in SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md does not apply here.
